clue.text: Tell-tale phone call coming earlier

indicators.note: says the call is placed ahead of the phone in the answer

parts.note: a whistle is a call or signal made by blowing
blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A sneak's phone call is placed before anyone else's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informers who expose wrongdoing; a tell-tale reveals secrets to those in authority.

clue.text: Indulge in feeble joke seconds before game against the French

indicators.note: places the earlier pieces ahead of the card game
means next to, so the French article sits alongside the game

parts.note: wet is British slang for feeble or weedy
a one is a joke, as in 'did you hear the one about...'
whist is a card game
le is the French masculine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone tells a weak gag just before a card game with French opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a drink, and drinking is a way to indulge oneself.

clue.text: Standard confession of a drug pusher?

definitions.meaning: a perfect model or benchmark to aim at
split as ..., a dealer admitting the trade

explanation.definitionFit: A model of perfection is a standard to be measured against; the split letters form an admission of selling drugs.

clue.text: Obsolete workplace supplied with plumber's implement by Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: piping is the work of a plumber
a tool is an implement

explanation.surface: An outdated office was handed some kit belonging to a plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is by sound: PIPING TOOL becomes 'typing pool', with the Y spelling the long I sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices once had rooms full of typists producing documents; word processors made such departments a thing of the past.

clue.text: See about 10ac? Given time you got it

indicators.note: the see goes around the remaining letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and see, or bishop's diocese, in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: time is added on to the cross-reference letters

parts.note: read literally: X is the Roman numeral ten, then the letters AC as printed

explanation.surface: Look up a cross-reference to another clue; with time you will crack it.
explanation.walkthrough: '10ac' looks like a cross-reference to FALSE, but it is read literally as X plus AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic agreement phrases, used to tell someone they are precisely right.

clue.text: Evergreen heather covering area with banks of scarlet

indicators.note: the heather wraps around the other letters

parts.note: ling is a common kind of heather

indicators.note: joins the area letter to the scarlet pieces
the banks of a river are its edges, so take the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An evergreen heather spreads over a patch of ground edged with red.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen figuratively means enduring or perennially fresh, as is something that endures.

clue.text: Wife's stern air

parts.note: aft means at the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: A woman's severe manner.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a gentle puff or breath of air carrying a scent.

clue.text: Confused older male with nothing for a benchmark

indicators.note: the letters are muddled into a new order
the circle meaning nothing takes the place of the letter a

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A muddled older man with nothing to show is held up as a standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing for a' tells you to put the circle in place of the vowel before the letters are confused.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplary person is a standard by which others are judged, so serves as a benchmark.

clue.text: A rethink in support — nevertheless stumped up

parts.note: to second a proposal is to support it
though can mean nevertheless, as in 'it's late, though'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders their backing but pays up regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped up' looks like paying, but splits into stumped and a turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a reconsideration after an initial decision, which is a rethink.

clue.text: Cast has inept point — that's actors for you

indicators.note: cast as in thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A theatre cast makes a feeble point — typical of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the definition with actors, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis was the legendary first Greek actor, so his name gives a word for stage performers.

clue.text: Simulated dives showing loss of heart and energy

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so a middle letter is dropped

parts.note: falls means dives or drops
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Footballers faking falls show they have lost both heart and energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simulated is fake or not genuine, which is a sense of untrue.

clue.text: Sample of unfunny long-winded material

indicators.note: Sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A specimen of humourless, verbose writing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synthetic fabric, a kind of material used for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Endless moonshine generating stimulating experience

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: moonshine can mean nonsense, which is tripe

explanation.surface: An unending supply of illicit liquor produces quite a buzz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moonshine' suggests bootleg spirits, but here it means foolish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a hallucinogenic or thrilling episode, a stimulating experience.

clue.text: A midsummer love that might be mine

parts.note: the middle of the word summer is its two central letters, MM
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A summer romance that could be one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks possessive, but it is the explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is an explosive, a form of munition, so it might count as ammunition.

clue.text: Mattresses given by Greek character for collection of complete idiots

indicators.note: the Greek letter collects, or gathers in, the next word

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
all means complete or whole
asses are fools

explanation.surface: Bedding supplied by a Greek for a gathering of total fools.
explanation.definitionFit: These are straw-filled mattresses, a cheap kind of bedding.

clue.text: Benefit from tasteless twaddle? The reverse

parts.note: a sick joke is tasteless

indicators.note: the chatter word is written backwards

parts.note: yap is foolish chatter

explanation.surface: Profit from bad-taste nonsense — or the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to an absent ill employee is a welfare or workplace benefit.

clue.text: Offshore bank said to be in credit before payment returned?

indicators.note: places the credit part ahead of the payment
the spoken word goes inside the credit letters

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
oral means spoken

indicators.note: the payment word is written backwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A tax-haven bank is reportedly in the black before a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offshore bank' suggests tax havens; it is a ridge in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge built by marine polyps lies off the shore, a bank in the geographical sense.

clue.text: Golf course's opening of dogleg is relative

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R and A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, Scotland, here loosely called a course

indicators.note: the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A golf course's first bending hole is linked to the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and A is strictly a club, not a course, as the blog notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Time to accept revival of support for refuge

indicators.note: the time word takes the support garment inside it

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

indicators.note: revival read as re-vival, a turning back, so the garment is written backwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: It is time to welcome back underwear as a haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A port is a sheltered place for ships, so a refuge or haven.

clue.text: Bowled wearing jumper with movement that's mechanical

indicators.note: joins the twitch to the end
the bowled letter is inside the jumper, as if dressed in it

parts.note: roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled while dressed in a sweater moves stiffly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, a British word for one; it is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Machine-like movements are stiff and automatic, like an android's.

clue.text: Shearer legendarily welcomed back outside left

indicators.note: the reversed word sits around the left letter
the greeting word is written backwards

parts.note: hailed means greeted or welcomed

explanation.surface: Alan Shearer, the footballer, famously cheered on his return out on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shearer' suggests Alan Shearer, the England striker, but it means someone who cuts hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible she cut Samson's hair, robbing him of strength, so she is a legendary cutter of locks.

clue.text: Old boy's back stuffing face with duck and game

the reversed letters fill the face word

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, O

explanation.surface: An elderly man is filling his face with duck and game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a juggling pastime played with a spool spun on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: Deposit found now and then in skillet

indicators.note: every other letter of the pan word is taken

explanation.surface: Residue is occasionally discovered in a frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine sediment laid down by water is a deposit.

clue.text: Billy Bragg originally in support group for Eurovision winners

indicators.note: the initials go inside the group letters

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a support group

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each name

explanation.surface: Singer Billy Bragg starts out in a self-help group for song contest champions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish pop group won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with Waterloo.

clue.text: Take care with answer that is in French for some

indicators.note: the that-is letters go inside the French word

parts.note: du is French for some, as in du pain
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Be careful with your reply, which is in French for certain people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are parting phrases; one says goodbye with take care, and this is French farewell.

clue.text: I fancy Anne, which may be foolish

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Admitting a crush on Anne might be silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb meaning to be attracted to, but it signals the shuffle.

clue.text: Director of Hammer film?

explanation.walkthrough: Hammer Films was a British studio famous for horror, so the clue suggests one of its directors.

clue.text: Scrounger given shelter by church

indicators.note: means next to, so the church letters follow

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A freeloader is taken in by a church.

clue.text: Ireland's head coach accepting a nil-one against Sweden

indicators.note: the coaching word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to coach is to teach
nil is zero, O
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

clue.text: Back judge's early maturity ignoring policeman ringing about uncivilised behaviour

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game
